Rice-Fish Post-Planting Summary

Author

as4538@cornell.edu

Published

June 3, 2026

Context

This report is a descriptive baseline summary of the rice-fish cofarming experiment participants. It summarizes the surveyed households/farmers, their living conditions, food security and mental health scores (anxiety and depression), plot characteristics, crop types, inputs, labor, and harvest outcomes. The statistics should be read as descriptive and exploratory rather than causal.

The sample includes 46 households across 6 villages.

Household Labor and Demographics

This section describes household composition. Children are defined as members under 18; adults are members aged 18 or older. Working-age members are aged 18-64.

The first table summarizes the household-level demographic structure. It is meant to answer three basic baseline questions: how large households are, how many dependents and working-age members they contain, and how much household labor is (potentially) available for work.

The next figure shows the average characteristics of individuals. Splitting each indicator between children and adults helps separate household labor availability from schooling/dependency.

The labor-demographics figure focuses on the distribution of household size, dependency, working-age availability, and work shares (family business vs. outside salary).

Living Standards, Food, and Health

This section summarizes living standards, water and sanitation, financial access, rCSI (food insecurity), GAD-2 (anxiety), PHQ-2 (depression), health and water exposure.

Living Standards

The living-standards tables summarize basic living standards, water and sanitation, energy use, and access to financial tools and community groups. The first table focuses on dwelling rooms, which is a key housing-density indicator. The second figure broadens the view to infrastructure, basic services, and financial access.

The next figure below expands the view to infrastructure, basic services, and financial access in overall sample distributions.

These household conditions provide context for the food security and mental health score distributions that follow.

Livestock

Livestock ownership and sales provide additional context on household assets. The table is descriptive by species is a complement to the living-standards indicators.

Food Security and Mental Health

The score distributions show the spread of rCSI, GAD-2, and PHQ-2. rCSI is measured at the household level, while GAD-2 and PHQ-2 are answered by the farmer only. The correlation plot then displays whether food security, mental health, demographics, land, housing, and financial indicators move together in the sample.

The following figure shows associations between the scores and household or household head measures.

These associations can help identify patterns for further discussion on the relevance of food security and mental health indices for the experiment.

Health and Water Exposure

The health table separates rice-field workers from non-rice-field workers. The survey did not ask these questions at the individual level (IRB protocol requirement on health information). The second table however shifts to the household roster and summarizes water contact by children and adults.

The household-level health indicators are complemented by individual-level information on whether members had water contact.

The health figure shows the distribution of health indicators at the household level.

Land, Plot Measurement, and Crop Types

This section uses GPS-recorded coordinates (through ArcGIS Survey123) as the preferred plot area measure, over self reported ones. Comparative analysis of both measurement types aims to evaluate farmer land perception accuracy.

Area Measurement

Household-level area comparisons are shown only for households with all plots mapped: a few plots could not be mapped due to the great distance from their respective households.

Among mapped plots, the next table compares the reported plot area with the GPS-based area (polygon) used in the production summaries.

The difference categories display the same comparison with bins that show the direction and size of reporting gaps.

Household-level comparisons are shown only for fully mapped households so that missing plot polygons do not biais total cultivated area.

The area-ratio figure shows whether reported areas tend to align with GPS areas. Values above one mean the reported area is larger than the GPS area and values below one mean the reported area is smaller.

Plot Characteristics and Crop Types

The tables describe the land characteristics and crop types and harvest over the three last season recorded through the survey. Numeric plot characteristics summarize the context, while recent-season tables show how plot-seasons are distributed across crops and seasons.

The recent-season table highlights plot-season outcomes over recall-period of agricultural activity.

The crop-composition figure shows crop types mix. It shows the overall crop focus and the season-specific focus.

Inputs, Labor, and Harvest Outcomes

This section summarizes input intensity, labor intensity, harvest output, and productivity among harvested plot-seasons. Productivity measures are descriptive and do not account for output prices or non-observed costs. Only harvested plots are included.

Overall Intensity and Productivity

This table shows five main indicators: input intensity, labor intensity, output per area, input cost per kilogram harvested, and kilograms harvested per unit of input cost.

Seasonal Patterns

The season-level table shows whether input use, labor use, output, and rough input productivity differ across recent seasons.

Crop-Level Patterns

The crop-level table pools harvested plots by crop to show which crops appear most often and how their average intensity and output compare.

Same production logic with average input cost per 1’000 m2 on the horizontal axis and average output per 1’000 m2 on the vertical axis. Each point is a crop type.

The appendix provides additional descriptive tables for readers who want to browse the underlying summary statistics in more detail.
